79. Male apoditerium (2): detail of the statue of Hermaphrodite. The gaps in the stucco allow us to see that he had his head crowned with bandages, whose tapeworms descend on his shoulders, but not to grasp the details of his face which nevertheless seems not to have the usual youthful features, instead being bearded.

80. Male apoditerium (2). The stucco artists, who belonged to a workshop of considerable level active in the last period of the city's life also at the Temple of Isis, solved the problem of the decoration of the lunette O interrupted by the arch of passage by preserving the succession of aedicules and pavilions as if the wall had been whole, representing only the parts that happened to be on the available surface. In the center there is a newsstand under which

81. Male apoditerium (2): detail of the S section of the lunette O with the cupid who is finishing wrapping a garland around the shaft that serves as a support for the aedicule with a coffered ceiling adorned with leaves. The retrospeccient Silenus has a pedum in his right hand and a pardalis on his left arm with which he holds a tray of fruit. On the large three-legged candelabrum placed on the right aedicule rested perhaps another figure holding the other end of the cloth.
82. Male apoditerum (2): detail of the central section of the lunette O with the Satyr holding a long drinking horn in his right hand.

84. Male apoditerium (2): detail of the S section of the E sub-arch with a two-strand braided frame (a motif that until now has only been compared in Herculaneum, cf. Mielsch, tav. 32.2) and a large vegetable candelabrum on a fluted base resting on circular feet.

83. Male apoditerium (2); in the E part of the room the decoration of the vault is essentially preserved in the S section where, from the impost follow one another upwards: a coffered consisting of two concentric octagons containing squares arranged by corner, in each of which there is a rosette; side rectangles with rosettes and trapezoids with birds in the corners (a pattern found in the vault of the tepidarium of the Terme del Foro); a rectangle with a barely distinguishable Nereid; two coffers with a branch also legible almost only in negative through the engravings of the drawing. The frames that frame each of these fields are ovoli. DAIR 771883

85. Male apoditerium (2): detail of the O side of the same section of the arch as in the previous photo; a Nike, completely naked since the drapery on which it sits has also fallen from its legs, guides a dolphin through the vegetable volute originating on the animal's back. A tongued frame finishes the edge, men193

86. Male apoditerium (2): the vault of the central room had a coffered motif of hexagons containing large corollas variously executed, closed at the bottom by a row of five squares with three squares on concave sides containing corollas, alternating with two medallions with cupids. The left one carries a shield and the right one a sword, and they both fly towards the center. The border along the arches consists of a band of different widths containing a laurel wreath.
87. Male apoditerium (2): a candelabrum completely similar to the one seen in subarch E is located in subarch O, has a more slender base and is preserved for the same height as the other.

88. Male apoditerium (2): detail of the O side of the same section of the arch as in the previous photo; a Nike, seated perhaps on the end of an opulent branch, holds with her left hand the volute rising from the back of the dolphin next to her.

89. Male apoditerium (2), part N of the vault of room O with a coffered of octagons separated by swastika meanders. In the lacunars, all with tabbed frames, trophies of weapons alternate with Maenads, Satyrs, Seasons, Erotes.

90. Male apoditerium (2), detail of the O section of the vault. The Maenad bears fruit in the mantle that she holds with her hands raised; The octagon trophy next to it consists of a bipenne, a pelta with a scorpion as an episema, a clypeus, rods, shields and a sword not visible in the photo.

91. Male apoditerium (2), detail of the O section of the vault. This lacunar is the only one of the third row preserved almost entirely, and it shows a helmet with lophos and paragnathids, a clypeus, a shield, two rods and a quiver.

92. Male apoditerium (2), part S of the vault with what remains of the octagonal coffered with trophies and flying figures, which were reproduced by N.La Volpe between 1856 and 1857 in pencil drawings particularly faithful to the originals due to that draughtsman's propensity for an academic rendering of the subjects depicted (see Disegnatori, p. 647,  fig. 90). AFS A1871
93. Male apoditerium (2), detail of an octagon in the lower row with a trophy consisting of two clypei and two rods.

94. Male apoditerium (2), detail of the O end: above a trophy similar to the previous one is a Satyr who, seen from behind, advances dancing with a plate full of fruit in his left hand and a rhytòn in his right held back and towards which he looks.

95. Male apoditerium (2), detail of a lacunar with a trophy quite similar to that of fig. 91 in terms of subject but with small variations and in the arrangement of the spears and in the treatment of the scorpion.
96. Male apoditerium (2), detail of a lacunar middle with shields, rods, a lituus (?) ending in a goose's head.

97. Men's tepidarium (3): the large room with suspensurae, visible due to the disappearance of the marble slab floor, had the basin leaning against the wall E which is the only one without niches, then walled up, recognizable on the other walls in the areas where the plaster is not preserved. The walls were also equipped with tegulae mammatae and the heat came from the adjoining calidarium located to the north. The door in the S wall allowed communication with the apoditerium.

98. Male tepidarium (3): the basin was covered with marble slabs that were removed after the eruption and one of them, evidently reused, left the imprint of an inscription dedicated to Augustus in his XIII tribunicia potestas, i.e. in 9-8 BC. The roof had completely collapsed and the course of the vault, partially rebuilt, was obtained from the kidneys and lunettes. DAIR 771897

99. Male tepidarium (3), N section of lunette E. The frieze on which the lunettes are set consists of a series of arched windows through which you can see triremes in profile. The windows are separated by caryatids and candelabra that support the frame with lesbian kyma above which is arranged the scenography with aedicules and thòloi within which were figures in various attitudes. An aedicule with a coffered ceiling and garlands is preserved, under which is a draped figure; Beyond the left wing, on a wall in opus quadrata, sits a man intent on reading a rotulo. As usual, the arch is emphasized by the frame of ovules and leaves. Minervini (BAN 1854, p. 148) described among the separating elements placed between the windows, in addition to the candelabra and caryatids of an archaistic type, also a figure in Phrygian dress (an Attis).

100. 7epidarium male (3), section S of lunette E with the same depiction seen at the opposite end, preserved in worse condition except for the detail of the central acroterium of the aedicule with a palmette motif. DAIR 771895

101. 7epidarium male (3): the frieze that ran along the walls separated a band with baccellato stucco placed below the impost of the vault and the covering of the latter that repeated, with wider strigilatures, the same motif. A small trace of the frieze is preserved on the S wall and the same motif of the triremes seen through arched windows, present in the lunettes, can be recognized. Minervini, who counted a sequence of seven windows, in the fifth instead of the ship distinguished the figure of a triton with a beard and coils of seaweed, who with his right hand held a whelk close to his mouth and with his left an oar, details documented by N's drawings. La Volpe (ADS 446 and ADS 453; see Disegnatori, p. 642, figs. 8384).

102. 7epidarium male (3): in the S section of the lunette O part of the frieze with the ships is preserved in which a caryatid and a candelabrum can still be partially recognized. In the highest part only a crenellated wall remains.

103. Men's Frigidarium (4): the circular room consisted of a central basin into which one descended through the masonry step, placed in correspondence with the niche from which the jet of the fountain came out, whose fistula had been removed in ancient times. The small step that runs along the walls was covered, like the top of the niches,

104. Male frigidarium (4): the decoration of half E of the room is known to us, as well as from the descriptions, from the reproductions by Niccolini (tavv. VI-VII) and by G. Abbate (Draftsmen, p. 418, fig. 245) which also include the two niches, which can still be checked on site, while the plaster has also fallen from the section of the wall. An elderly Silenus is lying on the balustrade of a large window through which you can see a garden with palm trees and flowering trees. A peacock and
106. Male Frigidanum (4): in the S-E niche a large marble amphora with a surface carved with leaves is painted.
105. Male Frigidarium (4): in the centre of the N-E niche, in a garden full of oleanders, among which birds fly, is painted a marble goblet crater that serves as a fountain. DAIB 772241

107. Male frigidarium (4): only in the cap of the S-W niche remain the remains of the depiction of the seabed with fish, also present in the others, and also documented by the 1:1 scale reproduction in a pencil on tissue paper by G. Abbate (see Disegnatori, p. 417, fig. 244).

108. Male frigidarium (4): on the sides of the entrance door located in the S part of the room, and in particular on the stretch to the right of the same, the remains of a "graceful female figure standing, dressed in a long-winded tunic and peplos" can still be distinguished. This depiction, perhaps nymph-fountain, was also repeated on the sides of the niche from which the water flowed, at least judging by Niccolini's description.

109. Men's Frigidarium (4): the O half is better preserved as regards the stretch of wall between the two niches and the stucco cornices that marked the impost of the caps: ovoli in the niches, kyma lesbius in the lower part and ovoli along the outer edge of the large protruding tuff cornice that belongs to the primitive organization of this environment. Evident traces remain of the double-arched framing of the niches and the red window on whose balustrade a figure seen from behind is lying.
110. Men's Frigidarium (4): the conical dome open at the top in a circular eye was painted in blue with a dense dotted with yellow stars with six rays arranged in orderly rows.

111. Male Frigidarium (4): the figure lying on the balustrade defined as a "nymph" (BAN 1855, p. 20), is probably a sleeping Maenad even if it recalls the statuary type of Hermaphrodite and is in a position of passage that would be well suited to the ambiguous being, of which, however, the dual nature is not visible in this painting. Two tall goblet basins serve as fountains on which birds have landed.

112. Men's calidarium (5): it is the least preserved room not only in this sector, but in the whole complex, due to the collapse of the floor in white marble slabs placed on suspensurae placed on bipedal bricks, the vaults and walls equipped with tubules for the passage of hot air. Of these, only the E one remains in its entirety with three niches, of which the arched power plant, in front of them is the heated basin, like the whole room, through the nearby frae furnium.

113. The female calidarium (9), well preserved up to the impost of the vault, has the basin at the bottom of the wall E, in the centre of the N wall the door to the tepidarium (10); The floor is white mosaic with a black border.

114. Female calidarium (9): detail of the floor with a carpet of white tesserae, a frame of black tesserae and a marginal flounce again of white tesserae arranged in a straight warp according to a widespread use from the second half of the first century A.D.

115. Female calidarium (9): the walls are covered with a low marble plinth, the middle area is painted red and divided by six pilasters on the long sides and three on the short ones. The pilasters are of rudented yellow stucco, and support white Corinth-style capitals on which runs a frieze with candelabra supporting garlands alternating with marshy landscapes with ducks and aquatic plants. A small frame with lotuses and shamrocks marks the attachment of the vault cladding in strigilated stucco.

116. Female calidarium (9): the plaster covering of the walls and the stucco covering of the vault was laid on a plane consisting of tegulae mammatae which, detached from the masonry structures, allowed the passage of hot air. DAIR 771939

117. Female calidarium (9): detail of the stucco frieze in the W section of the N wall with a duck among marsh plants, the pair of candelabra supporting the shelves of the lotus and clover frame from which the laurel wreath is suspended by means of a bandage, while a laid garland, which departs from the second candelabrum, is held in its beak by a duck in flight,  a motif that repeats symmetrically beyond a hanging clypeus that acts as a separating element.

118. Calidarum femminile (9): the basin is covered with large marble slabs and has an arched opening on the S side for the introduction of the testudo, a bronze half-cylinder which, connected with the praefurnium, ensured the maintenance of a constant water temperature. Placed at a slightly lower level than the bottom of the pool, it favored the exchange between the heated water that tends to rise and the cold water that goes downwards.

119. Female calidarium (9): in the W part of the room, near the wall where the only window in the room opens, there is the labrum. The total disappearance of the plaster of the S wall is already attested in a watercolour by G. Gigante (see Disegnatori, p. 1003, fig. 25).

120. Female calidarium (9), W wall: the stucco frieze still shows the marshy landscapes with ducks among lotus plants and candelabra holding garlands. Elements of the gymnasium are represented in the lunette: between two columns on which shields are placed and on each of which there is an urn, there is a competitive canteen, rendered in incorrect perspective on which pyxes, palm branches and bandages and a steamroller are placed; the cornucopia between shoots with a large design that closes the composition on the right had its counterpart in the incomplete part. The curved frame repeated the kyma with clovers and lotuses of the horizontal one.

121. Female calidarium (9): detail of the basalt labrum (?) on a cylindrical masonry base covered with plaster; inside the basin there are three circular recesses to place an ornamental element, a perimeter annular hollow and in the center there is the hole from which the heated water gushed into a small praefurnium underneath the outside of the W wall.

122. The female tepidarium (10) originally had the walls divided into niches that were walled up when they were covered, above the previous plaster of tegulae mammatae, to form a cavity, also extended to the vault for which the same expedient was adopted in order to ensure the heating of the room. The plinth was covered with marble slabs and the walls with white stucco on which thin columns stand out that support the lotus and trefoil frame.
123. 7Epidarium femminile (10): detail of the mosaic floor in which the tiles of the white field and the black marginal flounce are not arranged regularly.

124. Female apoditerium (11): the room, which derives from the transformation in the second half of the second century BC of a previous room, has on three walls the tuff niches intended to contain the clothes of the customers, and a plinth painted in red like the entire lower part of the wall. It was illuminated through two circular windows in the vault and a third splayed window on the O wall. The left door communicated with the corridor (12) which led to the secondary entrance 1st on the Via Stabiana, from the right one you passed into the fepidarium (10).

125. Female apoditerium (11): the inside of the niches was painted yellow, while the outside is red. On the pillars of the first three niches are graffiti large sailing boats and two birds, one of which rests on the nest (?). The frames above are lotuses and volutes and lotuses and shamrocks. The bezel had a white background.
126. Female apoditerium (11): detail of the pillar between the second and third niches with the graffiti of a ship with lowered sails and anchor lowered.

127. Female apoditerium (11): on the W wall was placed, after having walled up the niches, a masonry basin accessible by three steps, for the cold bath since there was no frigidarium in this department of the baths. The door in the N corner connected with the long vestibule (K) that led to entrance 48 on Vicolo del Lupanare.

128. Female apoditerium (11): the supply of water to the basin was ensured by a lead fistula placed in the hollow made in the floor, which dates back to the primitive construction phase of this room. Changes in the same are also attested by the cut still visible in the floor, along the N wall where a strip about 1.70 m wide has been filled with cocciopesto. 81 FU25950
129. Female apoditerium (11): detail of the floor in rhomboidal terracotta tiles arranged within a grid of white tiles, dating back to the second century BC DAIB 772264

1. Room (1): the presence of the steep wooden staircase for the mezzanine prevented the plaster from being spread over the entire N wall, which thus preserves its traces. Inside the same wall remains a terracotta pipe for the disposal of water on the upper floor.

1. Atrium (2): the holes for the beams of the floor, well preserved on the S wall, indicate the presence of an upper floor supported towards the N by vertical elements now lost, while the traces of a low partition inserted in the wall seem to indicate a different internal subdivision of the room highlighted by the fall of white plaster in the middle area and red in the plinth that first covered it. '79 N53795

2. Cubicle (3); the small room in opus incerta bore a decoration on a white background with orthostats arranged at the head of a schematic II style, now only partially preserved in the W corner of the plinth. 79 N54189

3. The triclinium (4) was covered by the floor of the floor above, supported by square beams housed in the special holes lined with bricks; the window drew light from the peristyle (19) of the nearby House of Siricus VII 1, 25. Traces of the purple plinth remain of the decoration.

1. The S jamb of workshop 24 was reinforced with the attachment of a sturdy brick corner resting in part on the ferrule of a small drainage arch probably made in correspondence with a channel or a pipe.
2. The small shop 24, consisting of a single quadrangular room, had the walls covered with cocciopesto, preserved in meagre shreds only in the N-W corner.

3. The entrance to workshop 26 was made of bricks and adhered only for a short distance to the oldest frame wall with long blocks of Sarno limestone. In the curtain there was a small square niche surmounted by a tympanum, in which an object was displayed that served as a sign for the workshop itself.  79 N54186

4. A sturdy wooden staircase, leaning against the N wall, led to the upper mezzanine consisting of a plank resting on beams, the largest of which remains the housing hole. A layer of cocciopesto covered the walls in opus incerta. 79 N54185

2. Vestibule (1): the cocciopesto floor with regular ornamentation of large white tesserae arranged at an angle dates back to the Republican age (II style). In the foreground on the right is the lava recess intended to support the closing bar of the door, in the background a manhole cover for inspection of the channel below coming from the impluvium, which protrudes onto the street, below the blocks of the crack.  79 N54083

1. The façade of entrance 47 on Vico del Lupanare has jambs and cubic capitals of limestone dating back to the Republican age (Maiuri RendNapoli 1958, p. 216, n. 26), on which there are scarce remains of the preparation of the plaster that covered them. From the street, following the path of the parallel rows of white tiles that dot the slightly sloping floor of the long vestibule, the gaze is directed towards the inside of the house, in particular towards the impluvium with its furnishings and towards the tablinum.  Below the blocks of the acripidine comes out the drainage channel of the water collected in the impluvium.

3. Vestibule (1): detail of the floor and the closing system of the door of entrance 47, with lava threshold and bronze hinges. The wooden door was decorated and reinforced with numerous bronze nails, 85 of which have been found.

4. Vestibule (1), floor, section E. Those who entered the house were greeted by a greeting form (Salve lucr, benvenuto, guadagno) outlined with small white tiles on the background of cocciopesto, datable to the Republican age. Few floor inscriptions have been found in Pompeii, and even fewer have been preserved; The threshold has also practically disappeared, adorned with a meandering and square motif outlined in white tiles, which marked the passage between the vestibule and the atrium.
5. Vestibule (1): graphic reproduction of the inscription and the threshold between the atrium and the vestibule.
7. Vestibule (1), S wall with room door (2) and rough plaster cladding.

6. Vestibule (1), wall N. The walls of the room are preserved up to the height of the second floor, which was practicable, and accessible by a staircase starting from the room (11); In the photograph the square housings of the floor beams are partially visible. The lack of the floor on the second floor accentuates the disproportion of the vestibule, which appears to our eyes longer and narrower than it really was.

8. Room (2), wall N with access door from the vestibule. The room has a simple decoration with a white background with partitions outlined in red: red are the splashes of color that create a decoration of pleasant effect on the plinth, red are the bands that identify the panels and compartments, red are the edges of the carpet. The twisted candelabra within the compartments, like the carpet edges that delimit the panels, are signature motifs of the Fourth Style.

10. Room (2), W wall with the large window open onto the alley originally protected by an iron grate and remains of a fresco of the fourth style with a white background. According to Fiorelli (Fiorelli, GdS 1862, p. 7) the panels contained in the center 'griffins, swans, thyrsis, vases and drinking horns, with festoons of herbs and hanging discs among fantastic architecture..', which we must imagine made as vignettes that decorated the environment in a very simple way.

11. Atrium (3), overall view from W. At the center of the vast room is the impluvium basin, whose covering with marble slabs dates back to the imperial age. Older is the mouth of a fluted travertine cistern visible on the right; In the foreground is an inspection manhole cover.

12. Atrium (3), overall view from E (from the tablinum towards the vestibule). In the phase that has come down to us, the vast room, whose roof, with four pitches open towards the center, rested on beams (Tuscan atrium), was devoid of rooms on the S side and had not yet been redecorated: the walls in fact retain only the layer of plaster preparation.
13. Atrium (3), N wall with the doors of the rooms (10), (9) and (8) and rough plaster cladding.

14. Atrium (3), S wall, covered with a counterlining in opus incerta. The latter has currently collapsed (1995), leaving the decoration of the previous, early imperial phase (purple middle area with yellow border; ovoli cornice) to emerge in the S section of the E wall. The beams were housed in the two deep vertical recesses to which the horizontal beams supporting the sloping roofs were fixed.

15. Atrium (3), frontal view of the impluvium covered with marble slabs; in the foreground the manhole cover for the inspection of the channel below; The table top on a grooved support dates back to the Republican age, as does the fluted travertine cistern mouth on the right. On the other hand, the parallelepiped support of a statuette-fountain (not found) covered with marble slabs dates back to the imperial age, whose waters must have poured into the basin (currently missing) supported by the grooved support located in the center of the impluvium.
16. Atrium (3), table top adorned with lion protomes, older than the fluted support on which it rests.

17. Atrium (3): the mouth of a fluted travertine cistern (upside down), like the table reproduced in the previous figure, is also older than the marble setting of the impluvium and still dates back to the Republican age. It was found broken and repaired in ancient times (Fiorelli, in GdS 1862, p. 7). 79 N54054
18. Atrium (3), cistern mouth.   79 N54055

19. Atrium (3): as soon as you entered the room (and immediately after passing the inscription Salve Lucru reproduced in fig. 4) you 'stayed on the theme' by seeing the block of lava to which the wooden safe was attached. The placement of these furnishings in the atrium is customary in Pompeii.
20. Cubicle (4), wall E with recessed for the bed and wall S: the cubicle, rustic, has walls covered with a high plinth of cocciopesto and the middle area with white plaster. 79 N54104
21. Cubicle (4), wall O with recessed for the bed and wall N. On this wall, below the rustic cladding of the last phase, the remains of a previous plaster emerge. 79 N54084
22. Room (5), wall N: a wardrobe has been placed in the space of a door connecting with the tablinum, which was later walled up; The wall is covered with white plaster.
23. Room (5), wall O: a small niche existing in the room has been filled in and covered with two successive layers of plaster, the last of which has a white background. 79 N54094

24. Tablinum (6): in the last phase of the house, the room did not communicate with the neighboring room (5), to which an open door in the wall $ led, which was later walled up and covered with the layer of plaster preparation. Like the atrium, the tablinum had not received the last wall covering. According to Fiorelli (Fiorelli, in GdS 1862, p. 10) the environment was inINS. 1, 25.47

25. Triclinium (8): the wall decoration of the room, currently almost completely bare as the elements that have not been detached from it are now completely vanished, is known to us in practice only thanks to nineteenth-century reproductions; the drawings and watercolours reproduced below (see below), which reproduce individual figurative motifs, can be completed with the panel by D'Amelio reproduced here, which shows us a decoration between the late III and IV styles.

26. Triclinium (8), N wall, section W. It is difficult to believe that this figure and the previous one reproduce the same wall, but some details that can still be checked in situ lead us to believe that D'Amelio's panel is faithful.

27. Triclinium (8), N wall, section O: detail of the yellow compartment of the plinth, containing a swan in flight with a ribbon in its beak, now completely vanished (see this detail in D'Amelio's plate in fig. 25). IV style.
28. Triclinium (8), N wall, section W: dark red predella, with birds bent down to peck. This detail is also exactly reproduced in D'Amelio's panel (see fig. 25). IV style.

29. Triclinium (8), N wall, central section: the deterioration of the colours allows us to better recognise the silhouette of the swan in flight with a ribbon in its beak and between its legs, made in the typical manner of the fourth style.
30. Triclinium (8), N wall, central section: detail of the predella with birds also reproduced in D'Amelio's panel (see fig. 25). IV style. 79 N54016

31. Triclinium (8), N wall, section E: the decoration is best preserved in this section of the room corresponding to the room proper, which received light from a large window in the E wall open onto the peristyle (19). In the center is visible the gap left by the detachment of the painting with Aeneas wounded

32. Triclinium (8), N wall, section E: detail of various elements of the decoration of the room: in the centre, the dark red predella with birds and grapes dividing the plinth from the middle area (also present in D'Amelio's panel reproduced in fig. 25); on the left, the simple pilaster that divides the decoration of the room from that of the antechamber; on the right, the twisted columns and the gate barrier of the middle area. IV style.
33. Triclinium (8), N wall, section E: black plinth with decorative element with concave sides ending in volutes. The circular guide lines are engraved with the compass. IV style. '79 N54022

34. Triclinium (8), N wall, section E: in the dark red predella D'Amelio's panel (see fig. 25) reproduces a scene of animal hunting (a deer fleeing in front of a dog), of which traces can barely be seen here.

35. Triclinium (8): the painting with Aeneas wounded, edited by a doctor and assisted by his mother Venus who arrives in flight and by his son Ascanius who wipes his tears with his robe, now in the Museum of Naples (inv. 9009), was located in the center of the wall reproduced in fig. 31. Diap. AFSN s.n.

36. Triclinium (8), N wall, section E: in the narrow compartment there is a stylized floral motif, in the black panel from two crossed thyrsis hangs a tambourine. Both these details are present in D'Amelio's panel (see fig. 25). IV style.
37. Triclinium (8), N wall, section E: dark red predella with birds. What still remains of the decoration agrees with the detail in D'Amelio's panel. IV style.

38. Triclinium (8), S wall, section E: the fourth style decoration of the room has completely vanished and can only be reconstructed on the basis of nineteenth-century documentation, from which it appears that in the center of the wall there was painting H, 1396. The painting, which remained in situ and lost, is known only from drawings ADS 493 and 494 (cf. also Disegnatori, pp. 396, fig. 218; 614, fig. 50). IV style.
39. The painting (H, 1396), a nineteenth-century representation by G. Abpresentant a young woman in fu- bate.
41. Triclinium (8): remains of a fresco of the fourth style on the pillar that divides the antechamber from the hall.  '79 N54029
40. Triclinium (8), S wall, section E: remains of the predella with birds. IV style.
42. Triclinium (8), S wall, section W with the lava threshold of the door communicating with the atrium (3). Decoration of IV style of the antechamber.
43. Triclinium (8), S wall, section O: detail of the volute border on a black background. IV style.
44. Triclinium (8), S wall, section O: detail of the dividing column between the panels and of the dark red predella with birds. IV style.
45. Triclinium (8), S wall, section O: dark red predella with birds. IV style.
